preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain owner privileges) to call includeInReward()
At least two addresses must be in the _excluded array
The address to be included (account) must be in the _excluded array

violation_target.exploit_hint: As owner, call includeInReward() on an excluded address that is not the last in the _excluded array. This will swap it with the last address but fail to update the mapping for the swapped address, causing _excludedAddressToId[lastAddress] to remain at its old position while that address moves to a new index. This corrupts the mapping and can cause issues in _getCurrentSupply() calculations, potentially leading to incorrect reflection balances.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The includeInReward() function has a classic array removal bug. When removing an element from the middle of the _excluded array, it swaps with the last element but fails to update _excludedAddressToId for the swapped address. This leaves _excludedAddressToId[lastAddress] pointing to its old index while the address moves to a new position, corrupting the mapping.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner. 2. Exclude two addresses from rewards. 3. Call includeInReward() on the first excluded address (not the last). 4. This will swap the first address with the last but not update the mapping for the last address, causing _excludedAddressToId[lastAddress] to remain at its old value while the address moves to index 0.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank to impersonate the owner. 2. Call excludeFromReward() for address A and address B. 3. Verify both are excluded and in the array. 4. Call includeInReward(address A). 5. After this, address B should be at index 0 in _excluded array but _excludedAddressToId[address B] should still be 2 (or the old index). 6. The oracle checks _excludedAddressToId[_excluded[idOfAccount]] == 0 where idOfAccount is the old index of address B.
